problem: Small-scale Vision-Language Models lack reasoning and thinking capabilities needed for reliable performance on proprietary tasks.
approach: DyME dynamically selects between memorization (SFT) and exploration (RLVR) at each optimization step, combined with a Visual Supervision mechanism to inject image-grounded guidance.
contribution: The method consistently improves small VLM performance across diverse domains by stabilizing the SFT-RLVR tradeoff.

problem: Heterogeneous treatment effect estimation from censored survival data is under-evaluated due to fragmented benchmarks and inconsistent methodologies.
approach: SurvHTE-Bench provides a modular suite of synthetic, semi-synthetic, and real-world datasets with known ground truth, enabling systematic comparison of HTE methods.
contribution: The benchmark offers the first rigorous comparison of survival HTE methods across diverse conditions and realistic assumption violations.

problem: Reward models for diffusion-based visual generation struggle with unreliable reward estimation on noisy latents and inconsistent preference rankings across trajectories.
approach: SLRM uses the diffusion model as a discriminator with learnable task tokens and score enhancement; TAPO performs multi-timestep reward evaluation with SDE sampling to capture trajectory advantages.
contribution: The framework significantly improves text-to-image and text-to-video generation by achieving noise-compatible and consistent trajectory-level preference optimization.

problem: Open-vocabulary detectors fail to generalize to real-world datasets with out-of-distribution classes, and real-time detection requires expensive retraining for new domains.
approach: RF-DETR uses weight-sharing neural architecture search to discover accuracy-latency Pareto curves, efficiently evaluating thousands of configurations without full retraining.
contribution: RF-DETR achieves 48.0 AP on COCO (beating D-FINE by 5.3 AP) and is the first real-time detector to surpass 60 AP on COCO.

problem: Masked Autoregressive models offer parallelism but their efficiency gains are constrained by the modeling complexity of spatially correlated visual tokens.
approach: GtR decomposes generation into two stages: structure generation establishing global semantic scaffolding, then detail reconstruction; FTS allocates more computation to high-frequency details.
contribution: The method achieves 3.72× speedup on MAR-H while maintaining comparable image quality (FID: 1.59, IS: 304.4).

problem: Homomorphic encryption enables secure LLM inference over encrypted inputs but imposes prohibitive computational overhead from expensive HE rotations.
approach: MOAI combines column and diagonal packing, introduces rotation-free algorithms for Softmax and LayerNorm, and uses interleaved batching to reduce HE rotations by 1.7× compared to prior work.
contribution: The framework achieves 52.8% reduction in evaluation time compared to THOR on BERT-base inference.

problem: LLMs are biased toward well-known generic algorithm designs rather than making creative leaps needed to navigate the discontinuous solution space of system optimization.
approach: MetaMuse uses three self-reflection principles: quantifying diversity in performance space, steering ideation via external stimuli, and constructing solutions via waypoint reasoning.
contribution: The framework generates high-performing algorithms for cache replacement (35.76% improvement) and online bin packing (30.93% improvement) at cloud scale.

problem: Large Language Models exhibit sharp performance drops when reasoning steps exceed training distributions, revealing a failure in reasoning hop generalization.
approach: The work identifies erroneous processing heads that amplify incorrect trajectories, then proposes test-time correction via dynamic head deactivation during inference.
contribution: The lightweight intervention consistently improves reasoning hop generalization across tasks and LLMs by restoring correct predictions.

problem: GRPO training of multimodal LLMs suffers from sparse rewards on difficult problems and advantage vanishing when group-level rewards are too consistent.
approach: DIVA-GRPO dynamically adjusts the difficulty distribution of variants for each problem and computes advantages within local and global groups using difficulty-weighted normalization.
contribution: The method addresses advantage vanishing and sparse rewards through adaptive variant augmentation while preserving full data utilization.

problem: The dynamics of feature formation during language model pre-training remain opaque, hindering understanding of how models develop capabilities.
approach: Using sparse dictionary learning (crosscoders), the work tracks linear interpretable feature evolution across pre-training snapshots to identify formation points and pattern emergence.
contribution: The analysis reveals a two-stage process: statistical learning followed by feature learning, with causal connections between feature evolution and downstream performance.

problem: Current value measurement methods for LLMs use outdated or generic test questions that capture only common safety values, yielding indistinguishable results.
approach: AdAEM automatically and adaptively generates test questions by probing the internal value boundaries of diverse LLMs through in-context optimization.
contribution: The method maximizes information-theoretic objectives to extract diverse controversial topics and track LLM value dynamics as models evolve.

problem: Language model outputs often require deterministic transformation to match downstream task requirements, but this coupling is not formalized as proper probability modeling.
approach: The framework composes language models with finite-state transducers to marginalize over source strings and propagate probabilities through transformations without altering model parameters.
contribution: The work demonstrates algorithms for converting token-level models to character-level or word-level models, and deriving amino-acid models from DNA models.

problem: Scaling behavior of parameter norms in overparameterized linear regression remains incompletely characterized, limiting understanding of implicit bias.
approach: Using dual-ray analysis, the work solves for closed-form predictions of norm scaling, revealing competition between a signal spike and a null bulk, with a universal threshold r*=2(p-1).
contribution: The unified solution characterizes all ℓr norm scaling for r ∈ [1,p] under ℓp-biased interpolation and predicts which norms plateau versus grow with sample size.

problem: Existing deep-research agents rely on a single expanding context window, causing context suffocation and noise contamination that limit long-horizon exploration.
approach: IterResearch reformulates research as a Markov Decision Process with periodic synthesis into an evolving report, maintaining consistent reasoning capacity via workspace reconstruction.
contribution: The method extends to 2048 interactions with dramatic gains (3.5% to 42.5%) and improves frontier models by up to 19.2pp over ReAct.

problem: Noise Contrastive Estimation struggles with accurately estimating ratios between distributions that differ substantially, limiting its use on high-dimensional datasets.
approach: Scaling the noise magnitude artificially aligns NCE gradients with Maximum Likelihood gradients, enabling trajectory-wise approximation from NCE to MLE with faster convergence.
contribution: Noisier NCE matches or surpasses SOTA on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet64×64 for image modeling while cutting training iterations by up to half.

problem: Multi-objective decision-making assumes static preference weights, but humans shift priorities dynamically as contexts change.
approach: Dynamic Preference Inference maintains a probabilistic belief over latent preference weights conditioned on context, updated from recent interaction and used to condition policy.
contribution: DPI adapts inferred preferences to new regimes and achieves higher post-shift performance than fixed-weight baselines across queueing, gridworld, and continuous-control tasks.

problem: Vision-and-language navigation agents suffer from catastrophic forgetting when adapted to new scenes, limiting long-term deployment across diverse environments.
approach: Tucker Adaptation represents multi-hierarchical navigation knowledge as a high-order tensor decomposed into shared subspaces and scenario-specific experts.
contribution: AlldayWalker learns continuously across multiple scenarios, outperforming SOTA baselines on multi-scene lifelong VLN.

problem: Sharpness-Aware Minimization's practical implementation approximates the objective through gradient ascent, but lacks intuitive justification for why gradients at shifted locations improve generalization.
approach: XSAM explicitly estimates the direction of maximum loss within the neighborhood and implements multi-level outlier compensation to address approximation inaccuracy.
contribution: The framework achieves better generalization by more faithfully implementing the SAM objective through explicit maximum direction estimation.

problem: Spiking Neural Networks lack robustness against adversarial attacks due to threshold-neighboring neurons that set upper limits on attack strength resistance.
approach: Threshold Guarding Optimization moves neurons' membrane potentials away from thresholds via additional loss constraints and introduces noisy spiking to transition firing from deterministic to probabilistic.
contribution: The method significantly enhances SNN robustness in adversarial scenarios while reducing gradient sparsity and state-flipping vulnerability.

problem: Multi-scale windowed self-attention in PDE foundation models propagates global coupling gradually, causing error accumulation and drift during long-horizon rollouts.
approach: DRIFT-Net uses a dual-branch architecture: spectral branch captures global low-frequency information, image branch handles local details, with bandwise weighting fusion.
contribution: On Navier-Stokes benchmarks, relative L1 error is reduced by 7-54% compared to attention-based baselines with fewer parameters and higher throughput.

problem: Standard monolithic world models struggle to capture diverse task dynamics in multi-task visual RL, leading to poor reconstruction and prediction.
approach: MoW integrates modular VAEs for visual compression, a hybrid Transformer with task-conditioned experts, and gradient-based clustering for efficient parameter allocation.
contribution: On Atari 100k, a single MoW agent achieves 110.4% mean human-normalized score (competitive with 26-task ensemble STORM) while using 50% fewer parameters; on Meta-World reaches 74.5% success.

problem: It remains unclear which factors most significantly impede LLM performance on counterfactual reasoning tasks across different modalities.
approach: A decompositional strategy breaks counterfactual generation into causality construction and reasoning over interventions, analyzed across 11 datasets spanning language, math, programming, and vision tasks.
contribution: The framework characterizes LLM behavior at each decompositional stage and identifies how modality type and intermediate reasoning influence counterfactual reasoning performance.

problem: Non-uniform quantization of large language models requires expensive optimization and fixed codebooks, limiting adaptability and efficiency.
approach: NuBitQ enables arbitrary bit-width, layer-specific quantization and introduces OCP that implements multi-level outlier compensation using weight perturbation, activation distribution, and propagation metrics.
contribution: The approach avoids costly Hessian computation and fine-tuning while offering strong scalability across multiple tasks and model series.

problem: LLMs exhibit reasoning mistakes from knowledge deficiencies, but diagnosing and remediating these in a label-free setting is challenging.
approach: LaMer uses relative entropy to diagnose deficiencies label-free, then adaptively synthesizes augmentation data based on severity and progressively remedies with curricular strategy.
contribution: The method improves various LLMs on seven OOD reasoning benchmarks with comparable results to labeled approaches using only 40% training data.

problem: Implicit reward models from language models generalize worse than explicit reward models despite being nearly identical, yet the root cause is unclear.
approach: The work reveals that implicit reward models rely more heavily on superficial token-level cues through theoretical and empirical analysis.
contribution: The findings demonstrate that implicit models generalize worse under token-level distribution shifts than explicit models.

problem: Theoretical understanding of which algorithms achieve both high accuracy and good calibration remains limited, especially in restrictive settings.
approach: The work provides a uniform convergence bound for smooth calibration error and shows that functional gradients control training CE, analyzed across gradient boosting, kernel boosting, and neural networks.
contribution: The framework derives conditions under which classification and calibration performances are simultaneously guaranteed with provable guarantees.

problem: Generalizing articulated object manipulation across diverse objects requires understanding functional parts, but lifting 2D features to 3D causes multi-view inconsistencies and low resolution.
approach: PA3FF learns a dense 3D feature field with part awareness via contrastive learning using 3D part proposals; PADP is an imitation framework for sample-efficient manipulation.
contribution: PA3FF consistently outperforms 2D and 3D baselines on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks with enhanced generalization.

problem: Guided diffusion sampling relies on approximating intractable likelihood scores, introducing significant noise into sampling dynamics.
approach: The method uses adaptive moment estimation to stabilize noisy likelihood scores during sampling with simple, drop-in modifications.
contribution: Despite simplicity, achieves state-of-the-art results on image restoration and class-conditional generation tasks, outperforming more complex methods.

problem: Vision-Language Models process visual information by serialization, diverging from human parallel vision and hindering deeper understanding of internal mechanisms.
approach: The work decomposes visual processing via dual-stream hypothesis into object recognition (text token maps) and spatial perception (derived geometric structure), with plug-and-play decoder for compression.
contribution: The analysis reveals two-stage visual processing from attribute recognition to semantic disambiguation, enabling efficiency improvements and spatial reasoning enhancements via RoPE scaling.

problem: Image autoregressive models produce outputs visually identical to real images, hindering robust provenance tracing needed to prevent misinformation and detect fraud.
approach: A post-hoc framework detects characteristic patterns introduced by generation processes as reliable provenance signals, requiring no modifications to the generative process.
contribution: The approach enables robust detection of IAR-generated images across a wide range of autoregressive models without watermarking.

problem: Developing foundation models for experimental particle physics is challenging due to sparse, spatially distributed detector data that differs from natural language.
approach: FM4NPP proposes a novel self-supervised training method for detector data with a dataset of 11 million particle collision events and task-specific adapters for downstream tasks.
contribution: With frozen weights and adapters, the FM consistently outperforms baseline models across all downstream tasks with robust data-efficient adaptation.

problem: Existing scene change detection methods fail to generalize out-of-domain and either neglect 3D aspects or require multi-view inputs, limiting real-world applicability.
approach: GOLDILOCS reformulates change detection as 3D reconstruction over time using dense stereo to estimate cameras and filter geometric inconsistencies, then detects changes via mask tracking and SSIM heatmaps.
contribution: The zero-shot, pose-agnostic method achieves superior performance on both pairwise and multi-view cases over prior work including supervised methods.

problem: Multi-armed bandit algorithms must enforce cross-context minimum reward constraints while maximizing cumulative reward, but lack closed-form optimal allocations.
approach: The work designs algorithms that either optimistically prioritize performance or pessimistically enforce constraints, with problem-dependent upper bounds on regret and violations.
contribution: A lower bound demonstrates that time-horizon dependence is optimal in general and reveals fundamental limitations of free exploration principles.

problem: Post-treatment selection in interventional causal discovery introduces spurious dependencies that mimic causal responses, distorting discovery results.
approach: The work introduces a causal formulation that explicitly models post-treatment selection via FI-Markov equivalence and F-PAG graphical diagram, with F-FCI algorithm for causal identification.
contribution: The framework characterizes Markov properties and enables identification of causal relations, latent confounders, and post-treatment selection patterns.

problem: KL-regularized policy gradient methods lack unified understanding of how different KL variants, normalizations, and estimators interact under off-policy settings.
approach: The Regularized Policy Gradient view unifies normalized/unnormalized KL variants, specifies conditions for gradient equivalence, and introduces RPG-Style Clip for stable off-policy training.
contribution: On AIME24 and AIME25 benchmarks, RPG-REINFORCE improves accuracy by up to +6 absolute percentage points over DAPO.

problem: Irregular temporal data with varying frequencies, durations, and missing values is addressed in isolation across communities, fragmenting tools and methods.
approach: PYRREGULAR introduces a unified framework and first standardized dataset repository using a common array format, with benchmarks of 12 classifiers on 34 datasets.
contribution: The repository centralizes irregular time series research and enables robust evaluation of temporal data analysis methods across diverse domains.

problem: Evaluating LLM/VLM capabilities for game-playing is fragmented, entangling multiple skills and hindering identification of specific performance drivers.
approach: LMGame-Bench provides a modular harness across six games with toggleable perception, memory, and reasoning modules; enables selective probing of distinct capabilities.
contribution: Evaluation of 13 SOTA models reveals limitations in visual state extraction, reflection, spatiotemporal reasoning, and long-context reasoning.

problem: Continual learning with structural regularization faces a fundamental tradeoff between memory complexity and statistical efficiency that remains uncharacterized.
approach: The work establishes upper and lower bounds on joint excess risk, revealing how increasing regularization vectors reduces memory but increases excess risk.
contribution: Theory shows structural regularization mitigates catastrophic forgetting and achieves comparable performance to joint training.

problem: Perceiving visual semantics embedded in text strings via ASCII art is an under-explored capability with no standardized evaluation for LLMs and MLLMs.
approach: ASCIIEval provides 3K samples across elaborate categorization with training data; evaluates models via text and image modalities to diagnose visual perception tradeoffs.
contribution: Analysis reveals proprietary models (GPT-5 tops rank) exceed open-source MLLMs by 20%+ accuracy; none benefit from simultaneous multimodal provision.

problem: Text-to-Audio generation lacks structured preference mechanisms and efficient models that can generate long-form audio in practical time.
approach: TangoFlux (515M params) generates 30s of audio in 3.7s on A40 GPU; CRPO iteratively generates and optimizes preference data using CLAP ranking.
contribution: The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on objective and subjective benchmarks through flow matching and CLAP-ranked preference optimization.
